instructions: You are one of two independent readers for a public record that scores theories of consciousness. A study counts toward a prediction only if that prediction was on record, in a dated publication by the theory's own proponents, before the study first appeared. A study that says it set out to test a theory tests nothing if the prediction was first written in the same paper (or the study's own registration). When the dates or the commitment are unclear, the study is not counted. Read the passages and dates. Decide: BEFORE (the earlier passage commits the theory to this prediction, and it predates the study), NOT-BEFORE (it does not), or UNCLEAR. Answer in JSON: {"verdict": "before"|"not-before"|"unclear", "reason": "two to four plain sentences", "unsure": true|false, "unsure_why": "..."}.

core_claim.quote: Ignition is characterized by the sudden, coherent, and exclusive activation of a subset of workspace neurons coding for the current conscious content, with the remainder of the workspace neurons being inhibited.

source.citation: Mashour GA, Roelfsema P, Changeux J-P, Dehaene S. Conscious processing and the global neuronal workspace hypothesis. Neuron 105(5):776-798, 2020

prediction.statement: When a stimulus becomes conscious, activity rises suddenly and late (about 250 to 300 ms after it appears) and spreads to prefrontal and parietal cortex; stimuli that stay unconscious do not do this. It holds whatever the sense, and whether or not the stimulus is reported.

first_stated.passage: conscious access is often characterized by a late non-linear amplification of activation which invades a distributed set of parietal, prefrontal and cingulate areas

source.citation: Dehaene S, Charles L, King J-R, Marti S. Toward a computational theory of conscious processing. Current Opinion in Neurobiology 25:76-84, 2014

prediction.test_for: Comparing physically identical stimuli that are and are not consciously perceived, the perceived ones produce a late (after about 250 ms), sudden increase of activity in prefrontal and parietal cortex, also when no report is required; or, where every stimulus is seen, each new percept produces such a response in prefrontal cortex.
prediction.test_against: In a design that removes the need to report, awareness-related differences are confined to sensory cortex, with no reliable prefrontal or parietal increase.

study.name: Auditory awareness without report, measured with fMRI (inattentional deafness)

source.citation: Dellert T, Balster H, Schlossmacher I, Bruchmann M, Moeck R, Straube T. Neural correlates of consciousness in an auditory no-report fMRI study. bioRxiv 2025.05.16.654468; published in Current Biology, 2025 (10.1016/j.cub.2025.10.026)

passages.text: This non-linear divergence occurs regardless of the stimulus modality or paradigm used to manipulate consciousness (e.g., reduced visibility, masking, inattention).

source.citation: Mashour GA, Roelfsema P, Changeux J-P, Dehaene S. Conscious processing and the global neuronal workspace hypothesis. Neuron 105(5):776-798, 2020

passages.text: GNW posits that every conscious experience is accompanied by activation of a fronto-parietal network in tandem with high-level sensory cortices.

source.citation: Melloni L, Mudrik L, Pitts M, Bendtz K, Ferrante O, ... Dehaene S, Koch C, Tononi G, Ward LM. An adversarial collaboration protocol for testing contrasting predictions of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theory. PLOS ONE 18(2):e0268577, 2023

dates.statement: 2013-12-29 (late ignition); 2020-03-04 (any modality or paradigm, including inattention)
